newsitem.title: BULGARIA: G-24 WILL COVER $500 MLN BULGARIA FUNDING GAP-EU.
newsitem.headline: G-24 WILL COVER $500 MLN BULGARIA FUNDING GAP-EU.

text.p: The European Union and other lenders will provide additional support of up to $500 million following Bulgaria's agreement with the International Monetary Fund, a senior EU official said on Tuesday.
"Most probably out of the whole IMF stabilisation programme there will be some $400 or $500 million to be covered still," EU External Affairs commissioner Hans van den Broek told a news conference.

"The European Union will certainly hope to make a substantial contribution to cover that gap but as always under the conditions and assuming that also the other G-24 partners are prepared to make a contribution."

On Monday, the IMF and the interim government announced a new standby accord and an emergency payment to buy grain, totalling more than $650 million. The programme must still be approved by the IMF board at a meeting next month.
Van den Broek said the EU would provide new macro-financial assistance to be discussed in parallel with approval of the IMF agreement. An EU technical mission is due in Sofia next week.
Members of the G-24 group of industrialised countries will make their pledges at a Consultative Group meeting in Brussels early next month before the IMF board meets.
Bulgaria's authorities have agreed to a tough programme of restructuring, privatisation and budget discipline, including implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime from June.
Unemployment is already 13.7 percent of the workforce, and the National Labour Exchange said on Tuesday the number of jobless could rise to 700,000 by June from February's 525,148.

"The people of Bulgaria already suffered considerably in the past and they are being asked again to show patience and forbearance before the benefits of economic stabilisation and structural reform are felt," van den Broek said in a speech at Sofia University.

He said the EU's Phare programme would help the authorities to implement reforms, and the EU would offer more social support in addition to 20 million Ecus ($22.8 million) for the lowest-income groups due to be disbursed next week.

Van den Broek said Bulgaria must restructure its industry and banking system, and urged tougher measures to protect intellectual property rights, singling out compact disc piracy which he said had cost the recording industry in Europe some $100 million.

"I have urged the government to address this matter in the interest of establishing proper market conditions and in view of Bulgaria's commitments as a member of the World Trade Organisation," he said.
"Confidence in the protection of intellectual property is a key element in attracting new investment."

He said Bulgaria needed investment in modern power generation capacity to enable it to meet international commitments on decommissioning units one to four of the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, which he said lacked "certain important safety features".
In 1993, Bulgaria received a grant of 24 million Ecus to help it prepare to close the four Soviet-made 440-megawatt reactors as soon as energy supplies allowed.
